messages.author: 8fe72476574bf468
messages.subject: TopN vs ALL and Individual vs summed ions
parts:
Dear Olga and co.

we have been performing SWATH-DIA experiments on human dendritic cells derived samples subjected to various treatments.
We are quantifying based on MS2 and we have done extensive work to clean up our transitions from interfering ions.
We are therefore quite confident of the quality of our transitions.

We are now in the process of deciding whether it would be best to use ALL transitions vs a selection of the TopN transitions (based on spectral library rank) and whether we should SUM the areas or use them individually for MSStats analysis.

Do you have any suggestions based on your statistical experience which of the four strategies is expected to give most reliable results?
These are the options we are considering:
  1. All + SUM
  2. All + INDIVIDUAl
  3. TopN  + SUM or
  4. TopN + INDIVIDUAL

Thanks for your help


Caterina

messages.author: 642c5a220db2f495
messages.subject: Re: TopN vs ALL and Individual vs summed ions
parts:
Dear Caterina,

My name is Mike Cheng working with Professor Olga Vitek, and I have been working on a feature selection project,attempting to remove the MS2 peaks with interference.

Perhaps Olga or some other members in our lab can weigh in later.

If you are confident that almost all the MS2 features with interference were removed, then it makes more sense to use all of the MS2 features. When it comes to whether doing the sum or using individual MS2 features, now even MSstats does (robustly) summarize the protein intensities at each MS run, as opposed to doing SUM, before proceeding to the downstream analysis.

My suggestion is ALL + MSstats, if the MS2 features with interference have been removed. Since you were thinking about taking TopN, there is an optional functionality in MSstats helps remove the features with interference, called feature selection, to be considered as a better alternative than TopN.



Regards,
Mike C.

Hi Mike,

could you explain why MSstats now uses a summary value per run instead of using the features intensities as given in the input? It seems like quite a drastic change in modelling philosophy to me, but there is no background information why this should  lead to better estimates.

messages.author: 085b00b73e467d88
messages.subject: Re: TopN vs ALL and Individual vs summed ions
parts:
Hi Tobi,

A reason is that features from one run are measured together (as a block), and it's important to partition the within-run and between-run variabilities accordingly, especially if they don't share similar characteristics. MSstats implements this idea by partitioning the variability into two levels, as a subplot to make a restriction on randomization and characterize the variability within runs, followed by a whole plot to characterize the between-run variability. 

Hope this helps
Tsung-Heng

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: TopN vs ALL and Individual vs summed ions
parts:
Dear Tobi,

To add to Tsung-Heng's comments:

There is indeed a big change in MSstats 3.0 and later. This is not a change in modeling philosophy, but a natural evolution. This allows us to express the experimental designs in a more appropriate and more flexible form. As Tsung-Heng mentioned, we now distinguish the within-run and between run technical variation. This also allows us to account for missing values and for outliers. There is a substantial empirical evidence that this is a better approach. We are now finalizing a manuscript that presents both the update to the models and the experimental evaluation. Apologies for not being able to make the manuscript available sooner.

Sincerely
Olga
